gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans reads straight and ruler-drawn, with a tall x-height filling the line. Plakkaat is best at heavy, closed letters curling nearly shut at the stems, while Vend Sans does open curves.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-alexandria: Pen-plotter smoothness defines Quantum, with loose, spacious letterfit. It does best as a clean display voice with open mouths, while Alexandria does best as tall, sans-serif text with wide terminals.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-amiko: Tech-clean and spacious, Quantum keeps its mouths open and its ascenders compressed. Amiko stands out for tall, crayon-thick lowercase with terminals pointing outward like tongs, giving the text real presence.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-telugu: Crisp and spacious, Quantum holds a tube-like thickness through every bend. Anek Telugu sets a tall-bowled, approachable rhythm, its rounds left unlatched, so long sans-serif text moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anuphan: Quantum keeps its strokes uniform, with no swelling or thinning anywhere in the letters. And Anuphan carries big round bowls and open curves with clear gaps, so extended text feels easygoing.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-arimo: Clean and tech-minded, Quantum spaces its letters loosely, with no swelling or thinning, like bent cable. Arimo gives a tall mean line in sans-serif form, so a modest size will do.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-armata: Contemporary through and through, Quantum draws strokes as plain as stitched thread. Armata lets its sans-serif lowercase fill most of the letter height, so text moves with generous gaps between characters.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-fresca: Quantum is best as a display face with loose letterfit and mouths that stay open. Fresca does its best work as sans-serif text, with no calligraphic thinning and short ascenders above big bowls.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-hind-guntur: Hind Guntur brings wide gaps between curve ends and stems, and its tall lowercase forms look like stamped metal type. Quantum, loose and spaced, gives it room to sound sturdy.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-hind-madurai: Loose and tidy: Quantum keeps its ascenders short while Hind Madurai fills the line with capital-sized lowercase. Both keep their curves open, so the two sit together with ease.
